clues: This city sits on the south shore of one of the Great Lakes. It is the largest city in the north-west part of Pennsylvania.
Winters here are harsh and snowy, but the summers turn warm. The lake shore spot helps shape this big swing through the year.
A Native group lived in this land till the mid sixteen hundreds. The city took its name from that group of first people.
Perry kept his flagship, named Niagara, at its home port here. That link gave this place its Flagship City name.
This is the Gem of the Great Lakes, a name folks use with pride. Its twin name, Gem City, points to its fine natural port.
